A client result, with the platform and the period attached

HVAC and plumbing company, Houston

Google Ads Search, May 2025 to February 2026, about $20,000 a month. Cost per acquisition down 44% and qualified leads up 60%, in an auction where the core keywords cost $45 to $80 a click.

Done by restructuring campaigns by job type, rebuilding tracking so a booked job and a phone call were not the same thing, a weekly negatives programme and steady ad and landing page tests.

Experience

Brands I've worked on

Fourteen-plus years across agency, in-house and freelance roles put me on accounts with very different economics: SaaS and subscription products such as Intuit QuickBooks, Skillshare and Pontomais, global consumer brands such as Shell, Timberland and Amazon Prime, home services companies such as an HVAC and plumbing business in Houston, and companies in telecom, education, healthcare and e-commerce. Through Underscore Marketing, a US agency, I also worked on oncology, rare disease and gene therapy brands.

What carries over to your account is pattern recognition: how a trial-to-paid funnel differs from a lead form, which conversions each business can actually measure, and where spend usually leaks.

Who this fits

Companies spending $3K to $80K a month

Enough for the flat fee to be a small share of the total, and small enough that one senior person can run everything properly. Below that, a setup or audit is the better buy.

Owners and marketing leads who want the operator

You would rather talk to the person in the account than to someone relaying their questions. Reports are written for owners: cost per customer and what changed.

Lead generation and e-commerce

Home services, healthcare, B2B and SaaS, professional services, online stores. Industry-specific pages are on diwizi.com.

How an engagement starts

  1. A short form. Spend band, site and what has been tried. I reply myself with whether it is a fit, what I would look at first and a price range; a short call follows if it makes sense.
  2. A fixed-price audit. Written findings ranked by impact: tracking first, then structure, then bidding and search terms. Yours to implement, with or without me.
  3. Build or rebuild. Tracking fixed before anything else, because every bidding decision inherits whatever the conversion data says.
  4. Month-to-month management. Weekly work in the account, a written monthly report, a call whenever you want one. Notice period instead of a contract term.

Questions people ask before hiring

How much does a Google Ads freelancer cost?

Management is a flat monthly fee set by scope, not tied to ad spend. An audit is a fixed price quoted from the form and credited against the first month if you continue. No twelve-month contract. The pricing page explains how each model behaves and what to ask before you sign with anyone.

What is the minimum ad spend you work with?

No hard minimum, but the retainer only makes sense once the account spends enough for the fee to be a small share of the total; in practice from about $3,000 a month. Below that, a one-off setup or audit is the better buy.

Who owns the Google Ads account, the tags and the landing pages?

You do, always. I work inside your accounts with manager access. Nothing is built in a container I control, so leaving me never means starting over.

Do you work with clients outside the United States?

Yes. Most clients are in the US, Canada, the United Kingdom and Ireland. I work remotely from Curitiba, Brazil, which overlaps most of the working day in both regions.

Can you take over an account an agency built?

Yes, and it is one of the most common starting points. The audit usually finds duplicated conversion actions, broad match on Smart Bidding without negatives, and campaigns organised by whoever built them rather than by what you sell.

Do you also run Meta, Microsoft or LinkedIn Ads?

Yes. Google Ads is the core of the work, and Meta Ads, Microsoft Advertising and LinkedIn Ads are added when there is a measured reason, run by the same person.
